items.snippet:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: REPLACE_ME
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cua
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: REPLACE_ME
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true

templates.gatekeeper_template:

kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRequiredSandboxSecurity
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "Sandbox pods must set readOnlyRootFilesystem=true"

ai_advisor.executive_summary: Three security issues found for Deployment target-cua in sandbox-cua: service-account token automount exposed, root filesystem writable, and setuid/setgid binaries present. Risk band: high (total 14).
ai_advisor.remediation_overview: All fixes require operator review or image/workload changes. Do not apply automatically. Confirm Kubernetes API needs before disabling automount, identify writable paths and move them to volumes before enabling read-only rootfs, and rebuild images to remove setuid/setgid binaries.

prioritized_groups.title: Service account token exposure
prioritized_groups.rationale: High severity and high blast radius; tokens permit cluster API access and should be limited first.

prioritized_groups.title: Writable root filesystem
prioritized_groups.rationale: High severity; making rootfs read-only reduces runtime attack surface but can break workloads, so validate before change.

prioritized_groups.rationale: Medium severity; requires image rebuild and testing, lower immediate blast than token/rootfs issues.

item_advice.explanation: Pod currently exposes a service account token (automount). This grants in-cluster API access if exploited.
item_advice.operator_impact: Disabling automount breaks any in-pod code that calls the Kubernetes API (controllers, leaders, admission clients).
item_advice.validation_advice: Search containers for Kubernetes client usage, confirm no init/sidecar needs token, and test app functionality in a staging namespace after disabling.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Mitigates highest immediate risk of cluster API compromise; validate because breaking workloads is likely.

item_advice.explanation: Containers mount a writable root filesystem allowing runtime modification of binaries/config, increasing persistence risk.
item_advice.operator_impact: Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem can break apps that write to /tmp, /var, /etc, or application directories unless writable paths are moved to volumes.
item_advice.validation_advice: Inventory writable paths (including mounts: workspace, artifacts), move writable dirs to explicit volumes/emptyDir, then enable readOnlyRootFilesystem and run full acceptance tests.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Reduces attack surface by preventing in-container modifications; address after confirming token changes to avoid simultaneous unknown breakage.

item_advice.explanation: Image contains setuid/setgid binaries which can be abused for privilege escalation inside the container.
item_advice.operator_impact: Removing these binaries requires rebuilding the image and may remove expected admin utilities; testing required.
item_advice.validation_advice: Rebuild image from minimal base, remove or replace setuid/setgid helpers, run integration tests, then deploy updated image.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Lower immediate priority than tokens/rootfs but required to harden image; perform as part of image lifecycle work.

ai_advisor.guided_operator_message: Review and approve the recommended changes in staging: disable automount if no API use, move writable paths to volumes and enable read-only rootfs, and rebuild images to remove setuid/setgid binaries.
warnings: Do not disable token automount without confirming in-pod Kubernetes API usage; it will break API clients.
Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem will break writes to /tmp, /var, and specified mounts unless moved to volumes.
Removing setuid/setgid binaries requires image rebuild and may remove expected admin functionality.
next_steps: Confirm whether target-cua requires Kubernetes API access and list containers using in-cluster client libraries.
Inventory all writable paths and verify workspace/artifacts emptyDirs cover needed writes.
Plan and build a new image removing setuid/setgid binaries; run CI/integration tests.
